neighbours.label: southern and eastern China and the Yangtze or Wu region (South China, East China Sea, Zhejiang, Yangzi)
fire: Monsoon floods hit the provinces of southern China every June.
The fishing fleets of eastern China work the coast from Shanghai southward.
Silk production in southern China dates back more than two thousand years.
Ships sailed the East China Sea carrying porcelain to Japan.
Lakes along the Yangzi floodplain were drained for rice fields.
Wu dialects are still spoken in the cities around Suzhou.
The Zhejiang coast is known for its tea hills and fishing ports.
Winters are mild in southern China, but summers are humid.
quiet: Winter storms often bring heavy snow to northern China each January.
The fishing fleets of northern Japan work the coast from Hokkaido southward.
Wheat production in northern China dates back more than two thousand years.
Ships sailed the Baltic Sea carrying amber to Germany.
Lakes along the Danube floodplain were drained for hay fields.
Mongol dialects are still spoken in the grasslands around Hohhot.
The Hebei coast is known for its salt flats and grain ports.
Summers are dry in northern China, but winters are bitterly cold.

short: southern and eastern China, Yangzi region
